clue.text: Agitating to get home for the cricket match

parts.note: at home means in
pro means in favour of, for
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Someone is stirred up about getting home in time for the cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket fixture, a sport played mainly in Britain and the Commonwealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitating for change is campaigning noisily, the stance of someone who objects and demonstrates.

clue.text: Term not applicable to the Lev ant

parts.note: NA is the standard abbreviation for not applicable on forms
the Levant, the eastern Mediterranean lands, lies in the Middle East, abbreviated ME

explanation.surface: A form-filler decides some word has no bearing on the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'Lev ant' is the Levant split by the scan; the region stands for ME, the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a word or label used for something, which is what a designation is.

clue.text: Anglo-Catholic affair?

parts.note: a Roman is a Roman Catholic
the Anglo church is the Church of England, CE

explanation.surface: A question about some business within the High Church wing of Anglicanism.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse clue order: Catholic gives ROMAN, Anglo (as in the Anglican church) gives CE for Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair is a romantic liaison between two people.

clue.text: Hair-style in order not over-confident

indicators.note: over in a down clue tells the solver to turn the small word not upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: confident means sure

explanation.surface: A hairdo for someone who is not overly confident.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'not over' as the word not turned over, giving TON, then SURE for confident. The definition is a hairstyle belonging to a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks in many religious orders shave the crown of the head, leaving a ring of hair.

clue.text: Old Persian city in the Southern States

parts.note: the States is the USA

explanation.surface: A traveller places an ancient Persian city in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Susa was the ancient capital of Elam and later a royal seat of the Persian Empire.

clue.text: Obsessive feeling about sitting tenancy

definitions.meaning: something that fills the mind to the exclusion of everything else
humorously, the occupation of a property held before anyone else arrives, like a sitting tenant's

explanation.surface: Someone is fixated on the question of tenants who will not leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as pre-occupation: occupancy that already exists, as with a sitting tenant. 'about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is a mental fixation, while the punning sense means prior occupancy of a dwelling.

clue.text: Communist beset by allegation suffers break-down

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the communist goes inside the allegation

parts.note: a deposition is a sworn statement or allegation
COM is the abbreviation for communist

explanation.surface: A Red hounded by accusations has a nervous collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Decomposition is the breaking down of matter into its parts, as in rotting.

clue.text: Brief preacher recognised as a national leader

parts.note: to brief someone is to prime them with information
a minister is a preacher in a church

explanation.surface: A preacher who briefs others is hailed as the country's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective (short) but is the verb, to prime.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of government in a parliamentary state leads the nation.

clue.text: Commercial declamation held in very high regard

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
an oration is a formal declamation or speech

explanation.surface: An advertising speech is greatly admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is the deepest esteem or worship given to someone.

clue.text: Farewell not in order for a great film-lover

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

indicators.note: order here is a verb telling the solver to put the letters of not in into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye improperly to a keen movie fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film-lover' is not a cinema fan but a screen lover: Rudolph Valentino, silent-film heart-throb. The letters of NOT IN are rearranged to NTINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph Valentino was the great romantic idol of 1920s silent cinema, famous for playing lovers.

clue.text: Recurrence of temper spells disaster

indicators.note: recurrence read as running back means the word for temper is reversed

parts.note: a temper or humour is a mood

explanation.surface: When a bad temper returns, catastrophe follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is ruin or a terrible fate, a calamity.

clue.text: When summer comes for the brave

parts.note: when, of a date, is in: in June
June is a summer month, abbreviated JUN

explanation.surface: Summer arrives for a courageous person.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'brave' is a Native American warrior; the dated word in the answer is now considered offensive. 'comes for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a Native American, used in westerns of a warrior.

clue.text: Pass a drink

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Someone passes a beverage along.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with kola nut.

clue.text: Municipal ups and downs

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same going up as going down

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Local government has its highs and lows.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic affairs are those of a town or city, its municipality.

clue.text: Regular meeting-place for Henry and Sally

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Aunt Sally is a pub or fairground game, so Sally suggests aunt

explanation.surface: A favourite spot where Henry and Sally meet up.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a traditional British pub game of throwing sticks at a dummy head; here 'Sally' calls up AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunt is a place someone visits frequently.

clue.text: Lie about record product

parts.note: rec is short for record, as on a recording device
a line is a product range

explanation.surface: Someone tells untruths about a recorded product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' tempts as untruth, but 'Lie about' means lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean back or lounge at rest.

clue.text: A model once generously pro portioned

parts.note: ex means former, once
ample means generous in size; the page's pro portioned is proportioned split by the scan

explanation.surface: A former fashion model with a curvy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a pattern or specimen to be copied.

clue.text: Joint team awarded the championship

parts.note: the top is first place, the championship
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A shared team wins the title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' is not shared but a cut of meat; topside is a lean cut of beef. 'awarded the' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a cut of beef from the hind leg, a roasting joint.

clue.text: Jewish ascetic inherently Conservative in basic nature

indicators.note: inherently means held within, so the ascetic takes the Conservative inside

parts.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect

explanation.surface: A Jewish monk is at heart a traditionalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence is the intrinsic nature or core quality of something.

clue.text: Telephone for the labouring class

parts.note: hands are labourers, farm or factory workers
a set is a class or group

explanation.surface: A phone for the working class.
explanation.definitionFit: A handset is the part of a phone held to the ear and mouth.

clue.text: Catch word, so it is rumoured

parts.note: to catch a remark is to hear it
a say is a word or voice in a matter, as in having one's say

explanation.surface: A catchphrase is what people whisper.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan ran 'Catch word' together as 'Catchwork'; the wordplay needs the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is unverified talk passed on from others, the stuff of rumour.

clue.text: Appeal to Land Girls for cereal

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in O God
the ATS, the Auxiliary Territorial Service, was the women's branch of the British Army, a land force

explanation.surface: A wartime appeal to farm women for grain.
explanation.walkthrough: Land Girls were women farm workers in Britain in the World Wars; here 'Land' points to the army instead, the ATS women's service.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal grain grown for porridge and fodder.

clue.text: What the ugly duckling became on the Nile

definitions.meaning: in the Andersen tale the ugly duckling grows into a beautiful bird
a city and dam on the Nile in southern Egypt

explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it is the bird of the fairy tale; as one it names the Egyptian city and its High Dam.

clue.text: Mark suffers a setback in school

indicators.note: a setback read literally means set back, so the word for mark runs backwards

parts.note: to note something is to mark it

explanation.surface: A pupil's grade takes a downturn at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is the famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Worst way to conduct

definitions.meaning: a verb: to worst is to defeat
a conductor's baton marks the rhythm of the music

explanation.definitionFit: To defeat an opponent is to overcome them; a conductor keeps time with strokes of the baton.

clue.text: First offender in prison to take a leading role

definitions.meaning: British prison slang for a first-time inmate
a verb: to headline a film or play

explanation.definitionFit: Prison slang names a first-timer so; to headline a cast is to be its lead performer.

clue.text: Rejecting sin in limited measure leads to timely improvement

indicators.note: in places the turned-round sin inside the measure

parts.note: moderation is keeping within limits

indicators.note: rejecting suggests throwing back, so the word sin runs backwards

explanation.surface: Turning away from sin in moderation leads to progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejecting' signals the small word sin turned back to front before it is placed in the measure; 'leads to' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Modernisation is updating something to current standards, an improvement in step with the times.

clue.text: Metal measure used as a balance

parts.note: steel is a metal alloy
a yard is a measure of length

explanation.surface: A metal rule serves as a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelyard is a weighing device with a sliding weight on a lever arm.
